rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's thirteen builder trees go (a row of eucalyptus, ficus and jacarandas along the back fences, a magnolia 3 m from a house front, a coral by a patio set); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the swing set, the patio set, the open lot corner, and two more in the back yards.

trees.why: the back yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): shade over the swings
the west yard with the patio set (1.4 m off): a coral tree over the table
the open lot corner at the north-west, 24 m from the walls: a full jacaranda
the north back lot line, 10 m from the houses: an old ficus between two yards
the east back yard of the south row, 5.5 m from the house, 44 m from the swing-set tree
